methodology: Source observations fact-checked against source sites or primary government documents in October 2026. 'Institutional context' is explicitly distinct from verified girls-softball program history; unverified topics remain publication blockers under the 38-dimension first-release contract. This sourcebook is not a sitemap, approved profile, media permission or 2027 schedule.

records.claim: Shiner ISD dates its community school-building history to 1890 and says it opened the present 510 CR 348 campus beside Comanche Stadium in 2007; a junior-high building followed in 2018.
records.caution: 1890 is not the foundation date of girls softball. Campus location beside Comanche Stadium does not identify the softball diamond or public parking.

records.claim: The school's current public softball page identifies Jason Keller, Anastacia Rehak, Patrick Walker and Kailey Moeller as the Lady Comanches coaching group.
records.caution: Do not infer separate coaching job titles for each assistant or a binding spring 2027 appointment.

records.claim: UIL's 2014–15 Shiner softball state-team sheet identifies Steven Cerny as coach, John Hoelter as assistant and Shiner's 2015 state-tournament appearance.
records.caution: Do not assign 2015 coaching history to Jason Keller or confuse the state-team sheet's prefinal record with a finished season.

records.claim: UIL's 2023–24 state-team archive identifies Jason Keller as head coach and Anastacia Rehak and Patrick Walker as assistants; its earlier-edition record lists 13 tournament appearances through 2024.
records.caution: The 2024 appearance count was a historical snapshot and does not replace the 2026 archive's 15 appearances.

records.claim: UIL's 2024–25 Shiner team sheet identifies Jason Keller as coach and records Shiner's 14th state-tournament appearance.
records.caution: Its 30–5 submitted season record is not automatically a postfinal tally; Shiner finished runner-up in the championship bracket.

records.claim: Pearland High School states that it was established in 1937–38, uses maroon, white and accent black, calls its mascot Derrick, and identifies its yearbook as The Gusher.
records.caution: 1937–38 is the SCHOOL's founding period, not evidence of when its softball program began; the mascot named Derrick is the wider school's mascot, not a player or facility.

records.claim: Pearland High publishes separate fight-song and school-song traditions as part of its campus profile and uses Pride, Honor and Success as its motto.
records.caution: School traditions supply contextual identity but must not be presented as softball-team-specific rituals without team reporting. Do not reproduce song lyrics.

records.claim: Pearland ISD's June 3, 2026 story documents a 6–3 title-game win over Waco Midway and Pearland state softball titles in 1996, 2010, 2023 and 2026.
records.caution: The district story spells the coach's given name Michelle; its current school sports department spells Michele. Cite variants by source, prefer school department for current role.

records.claim: Pearland High's own athletics general-information directory identifies Michele Hyden as girls athletics coordinator.
records.caution: Athletics coordinator is not itself a date-specific 2027 head softball coaching appointment, even though a separate softball staff page lists her as head coach.

records.claim: Pearland High's school softball ticketing page displays May 2026 playoff dates at A&M Consolidated in College Station and a Game 3 note naming a different opponent.
records.caution: This is an historical away-site playoff notice and inconsistent opponent listing; it is neither the home softball-field address nor a published 2027 varsity schedule.

records.claim: Pearland ISD lists PHS Youth Softball Camp and PHS Future Softball Players among district youth camp offerings, distinguishing those school-led programs from unrelated community select-ball leagues.
records.caution: The offerings are 2026 listings and not evidence of registrations, prices, current availability or school attendance eligibility for next summer.

records.claim: Katy ISD's October 10, 2025 Athletic Hall of Honor induction included the entire 2015 Katy High softball state championship team and separately recognized Coach Kalum Haack as an individual honoree.
records.caution: The page includes separate football inductees. Do not imply its football team or all named individuals were members of the softball program.

records.claim: Katy ISD's 2026 championship story confirms a 7–2 victory against Forney, its 2015, 2019 and 2026 state title seasons and the postfinal 39–5 team record.
records.caution: The UIL submitted team sheet lists 38–5 before the title game, a date-cutoff difference, not contradictory accounts.

records.claim: Katy ISD's July 27, 2026 official board-meeting video index includes agenda item 9.11 to consider naming part of a Katy High School facility.
records.caution: An agenda entry alone is not an adopted vote or proof of the exact installed naming/sign text; verify official minutes or recording before elevating the field honor.

records.claim: Texas House Resolution 1528 commemorates Ganado's first UIL state softball championship in 2025, a 5–4 final against Riesel, a 33–5–1 final record and 10–0 postseason.
records.caution: These are 2024–25 facts; do not transfer this record to 2025–26 or conflate the first title with its 2026 repeat.

records.claim: Ganado ISD lists the high school and junior high at 501 W Devers, while district administration uses 210 S 6th Street.
records.caution: Neither 501 W Devers nor the district office automatically provides the entrance or exact playing address of Ganado Softball Field.

records.claim: Ganado High publishes athletics events and school contacts, but its general homepage currently emphasizes October-season events rather than confirmed spring-2027 varsity softball field entry details.
records.caution: Do not infer field accessibility, ticket costs, event parking or a game calendar from general high-school information.

records.claim: Amarillo Highland Park ISD's live feed refers to softball and baseball as its two newest programs and records a parent softball meeting in older school announcements.
records.caution: The relative displayed age ('almost two years ago') is not a precise launch date; do not copy Dallas Highland Park athletics information.

records.claim: Highland Park ISD's official Amarillo site is hpisd.net, with administrative address 15300 Amarillo Blvd East; it identifies its school community as the Hornets.
records.caution: Do not confuse this with Dallas Highland Park's hpisd.org, different student body and separate athletics/fields. District office address is not a verified softball venue.
